Flow: Bahá'í Funds (members-only contributions). Stated purpose: They support the Faith's work.. How it controls: They are genuinely a safeguard: refusing outside money prevents donor capture — and giving amounts are confidential.. Who benefits: The institutions benefit, and no individual clergy salary exists..

Flow: Huqúqu'lláh (19% of surplus wealth). Stated purpose: It is the Right of God, paid to the Faith's head.. How it controls: It is a substantial obligatory payment, though no source on this page records how it is assessed or accounted for.. Who benefits: The proceeds go to the Universal House of Justice's funds..

Flow: Volunteer service and pioneering (moving to another place to teach the Faith). Stated purpose: They spread the Faith.. How it controls: Committed members are expected to give substantial unpaid labor and to relocate.. Who benefits: The institutional expansion plans benefit..

Flow: Institute materials and training. Stated purpose: They support the study circles.. How it controls: Costs are modest, and commercial extraction is low compared with most traditions here.. Who benefits: The Faith's publishing arms benefit..
